title: European Union — Central Africa, "Digital Business Boost for Africa" grant, 2026
description:
"La Digital Business Boost for Africa contribuera … à renforcer les fondements d'une économie numérique sûre, inclusive et durable. Financée par l'UE à hauteur de 15 millions d'euros (9,83 milliards de F) et mise en oeuvre par la Banque polonaise, elle va couvrir plusieurs pays dont le Cameroun, le Gabon, la République démocratique du Congo et le Congo." (Digital Business Boost for Africa will help strengthen the foundations of a safe, inclusive and sustainable digital economy. Funded by the EU at EUR 15 million (FCFA 9.83bn) and implemented by the Polish bank, it will cover several countries including Cameroon, Gabon, DR Congo and Congo.)

Tagged `XCA` (Central Africa) rather than `CMR` alone: the source names four countries, all Central African, meeting the three-or-more-country threshold for a regional place code (`facets.md` §1). One of three EU-Cameroon grant conventions signed 2026-06-16 in Yaoundé; see also the companion CMR-only slice (2026-06-16-european-union-cmr-2026-acceleration-numerique-cameroun). The implementing Polish bank is not named in the source, so no vendor entity is tagged.

title: Benchmarking of ICTs in Central Africa
description: ITU project to conduct ICT benchmarking for Central African countries. Covers data collection analysis and dissemination of ICT indicators for policy and regulatory decision-making. Supports evidence-based digital transformation planning through standardized measurement methodologies. All target countries are SSA: Cameroon Central African Republic Chad Congo DRC Equatorial Guinea Gabon South Sudan.
recipient_organisation: CEMAC telecom regulators; national statistics offices
